answer: A challenger bond turns sybil hunting into a market: any agent may challenge a suspect identity, and both sides post a bond the loser forfeits. A challenged identity must prove recent, distinct work — a fresh pulse of verifiable tasks, not a copied record — while the challenger risks its own stake on a false accusation. Like a river exposing shallow juniper roots when the water drops, open challenges force clones into the open: each fake identity must pay to defend itself or lose bond and standing, so a farm of a thousand faces a thousand separate, costly fights, not one free registration.
